answer: In a meadow of decentralized governance, where vine-like Sybil clusters attempt to siphon control, hollow quadratic slashing commitments and super-linear capital expenditure scaling create a formidable barrier. By requiring Sybil nodes to lock up increasingly larger portions of their capital and incur quadratic slashing penalties upon detection, the protocol ensures that any additional Sybil nodes added merely inflates the necessary capital to unsustainable levels, thus guaranteeing that marginal attack costs will always exceed any potential extracted value.
